title: 3D Atlas: Redi’s Three-Jar Controlled Experiment
question: Why do maggots appear only on meat that adult flies can physically touch, even when air circulates freely through fine gauze?
explanation: Rotating Redi’s three glass jars in 3D shows that the gauze-covered jar admits scent and oxygen while blocking adult Sarcophaga flies, proving that maggots hatch from laid eggs rather than arising spontaneously from decaying meat.
limits: Displayed fly trajectories and larval growth rates are scaled for visual clarity.

title: 3D Atlas: Hooke & Leeuwenhoek Optical Bench
question: How did a tiny single glass bead lens outperform larger early compound microscopes to reveal living bacteria?
explanation: Exploding the brass paddle and cork specimen stage in 3D shows how Leeuwenhoek’s short-focal-length spherical glass bead achieved 270× magnification with ~1.3 µm resolution, whereas Hooke’s two-lens compound tube magnified cork cell walls at ~30×.
limits: Chromatic and spherical aberrations are summarised via the Rayleigh resolution limit.

title: 3D Atlas: Pasteur’s Swan-Neck Gravity Trap
question: How does a curved glass neck allow oxygen in while keeping boiled nutrient broth sterile for years until tilted?
explanation: In the 3D swan-neck flask, airborne dust and bacterial spores settle by gravity into the lowest U-bend of the glass tube. Only when you tilt the flask past 42° does sterile broth wash into the bend and carry trapped microbes back into the bulb.
limits: Spore settling is modelled as deterministic trapping at the lowest bend.

title: 3D Atlas: Eleven Orders of Magnitude of Life
question: Why must we switch from the naked eye to light microscopy and then electron microscopy as we zoom from a blue whale down to a DNA helix?
explanation: Sweeping the logarithmic 3D scale dial across eleven orders of magnitude compares specimen dimensions against the wavelength of visible light (~400–700 nm), showing why viruses and ribosomes require electron beams.
limits: Organism and macromolecule meshes are shown normalized inside the 3D comparison stage.

title: 3D Atlas: Monsoon Seed Imbibition & Turgor
question: How does a dry moong seed generate several megapascals of swelling pressure before its first mitotic division?
explanation: Slicing the 3D seed coat shows hydrophilic starch and protein colloids drawing water down a steep matric potential gradient (Ψ_m ≈ −3.6 MPa), swelling the cotyledons and splitting the testa so the radicle can emerge.

title: 3D Atlas: Candle Combustion vs Seed Metabolism
question: Why does burning glucose in a flame release 2,870 kJ mol⁻¹ entirely as heat, whereas a living seed captures ~39% in ATP at 28 °C?
explanation: Comparing the chaotic 3D combustion plume on the left with the enzyme-guided 3D metabolic staircase on the right shows how activation barriers prevent a runaway thermal explosion and channel free energy into ATP synthesis.
limits: Thermodynamic efficiency is modelled around standard cellular phosphorylation potentials.

title: 3D Atlas: Subbarow’s ATP Triphosphate Spring
question: What makes the terminal γ-phosphate bond of ATP a universal energy currency in every living cell?
explanation: Exploding the 3D ATP molecule reveals three negatively charged phosphate oxygens crowded together; cleaving the terminal γ-phosphate relieves electrostatic repulsion and stabilises the products by resonance and hydration.
limits: Ball-and-stick coordinates represent heavy-atom centres without explicit solvent shells.

title: 3D Atlas: Coupled MRS GREN Free-Energy Gears
question: How do the seven MRS GREN life processes couple downhill respiration (ΔG < 0) to uphill growth, movement, and active transport?
explanation: Meshing the downhill ATP hydrolysis drive gear (ΔG = −30.5 kJ mol⁻¹) with the uphill synthesis gear in 3D demonstrates that the combined cellular engine turns spontaneously whenever ΔG_net = ΔG_drive + ΔG_load < 0.
limits: Mechanical torque analogy for chemical potential coupling on a shared enzyme active site.

title: 3D Atlas: Why Viruses Need a Host Cell’s ATP Engine
question: Why is an isolated virus crystal metabolically inert outside a host cell while a bacterium or seed cell is alive?
explanation: Inspecting the 3D ATP triphosphate spring and coupled metabolic gears shows why a capsid lacking ribosomes and ATP synthesis must hijack a host cell’s free-energy engine to replicate.
limits: Focuses on the ATP and coupled-gear machinery absent from virions.

title: 3D Atlas: Eukaryotic Cell Wall, Vacuole & Organelle Cutaway
question: How do the cellulose cell wall, central tonoplast vacuole, chloroplasts, mitochondria, ER, and Golgi fit together in 3D space?
explanation: Switching between Solid, X-ray, and Section cutaway views of the 3D cell lets you explode the cellulose wall, central vacuole, nucleus, rough ER, Golgi, mitochondria, and chloroplasts.

title: 3D Atlas: Margulis’s Endosymbiosis & Double-Membrane Clues
question: What 3D structural clues inside mitochondria and chloroplasts prove they were once free-living bacteria?
explanation: Comparing the 3D prokaryote and sectioned eukaryote while exploding the mitochondrion and chloroplast reveals their double membranes, circular DNA genomes, and 70S ribosomes championed by Lynn Margulis.

title: 3D Atlas: Surface-to-Volume Diffusion Limit Cube
question: Why must metabolically active cells remain microscopic or fold their membranes as an organism grows?
explanation: Growing the 3D cell cube from L = 10 µm to 100 µm while slicing it in Section mode reveals the unreached anoxic core: surface area scales as 6L² while metabolic volume scales as L³, dropping SA:V = 6/L.
limits: Fickian diffusion depth modelled for cubic/spherical geometry without cytoplasmic streaming.

title: 3D Atlas: Endomembrane Postal Route & Specialised Secretory Cells
question: How does tuning surface-to-volume ratio and endomembrane ER-to-Golgi vesicle traffic adapt specialised cells to their jobs?
explanation: Tracking 3D transport vesicles from nuclear envelope and rough ER through cis-to-trans Golgi cisternae to the plasma membrane shows how specialised secretory and absorptive cells organise their internal machinery.

title: 3D Atlas: Fluid-Mosaic Phospholipid Bilayer & Fickian Diffusion
question: Why do amphipathic phospholipids self-assemble into a 4 nm bilayer that blocks ions while letting O₂ and CO₂ diffuse down their concentration gradients?
explanation: Slicing the 3D phospholipid bilayer reveals polar phosphate heads facing water on both surfaces and a 3 nm non-polar hydrocarbon core that repels hydrated ions unless a protein channel spans the membrane.
limits: Acyl tail thermal jitter is represented by harmonic oscillation.

title: 3D Atlas: Agre’s Aquaporin-1 Single-File Water Channel
question: How does an aquaporin channel pass 10⁹ water molecules per second while blocking smaller hydronium protons (H₃O⁺)?
explanation: Exploding the 3D Aquaporin-1 hourglass pore exposes the central Asn-Pro-Ala (NPA) selectivity constriction, which flips each H₂O dipole halfway through and breaks the proton-wire hydrogen-bond chain.
limits: Single monomer pore shown from the homotetrameric assembly.

title: 3D Atlas: Red Blood Cell vs Plant Cell in Osmotic Media
question: Why does pure water burst a human red blood cell (haemolysis) yet make a walled plant cell firm and turgid?
explanation: Comparing the wall-less 3D biconcave erythrocyte against the walled plant cell side-by-side shows how the cellulose wall builds positive turgor pressure (+Ψ_p) to balance negative Ψ_s in hypotonic media.
limits: Cell volume bounds clamped at haemolysis and plasmolysis thresholds.

title: 3D Atlas: Skou’s Na⁺/K⁺-ATPase & Active Root Ion Uptake
question: How do ATP-driven primary pumps and root-hair carrier proteins accumulate ions against steep electrochemical gradients?
explanation: Animating Jens Christian Skou’s ATP-driven E1–E2 rocker-switch pump in 3D demonstrates how phosphorylation switches conformation and affinity to pump ions uphill across the plasma membrane.
limits: Conformational tilt simplified to two rigid-body α-helical bundles.
